paragraphs: Mentioned in [Chullin 95b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.95b.19): he lost some tekhelet, blue-dyed wool, and afterwards found it. It had no identifying mark; he recognized it only by sight. He went to Rav Chisda to ask whether it was fit for use.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Visual recognition is distinguished from an identifying mark. The notice asks about fitness without giving the ruling.

In the linked Gemara, Rav Chisda asks about an identifying mark and then about recognition by sight. When Rav Natan says he can recognize the wool, Rav Chisda tells him to take it. Hyman ends his notice at the question.
